template_params.stores: physical stores open on at least one day of the window

prompt: Marieke, the CFO, is preparing a store benchmark for the bank's 2026 credit line review and asks for each physical store's net revenue per day it was open in 2024, the last year with audited accounts, so a store that opened during the year is not judged on days it did not trade. Take every store except the webshop (store_type web) that was open on at least one day from 1 January to 31 December 2024. A store's open days in 2024 run from its opened_on, or from 1 January 2024 if it opened earlier, to its close_date, or to 31 December 2024 if it has none or closed later, both days included. A store's net revenue is the sum of each line's quantity times its unit_price_eur, minus that line's line_discount_eur, over the lines of its orders with an order_ts on a UTC day of 2024; order_ts holds UTC time. A store with no such order has a net revenue of 0. Return one row for each of those stores, with four columns in this order: store_code; open_days; net_revenue_eur, not rounded; and revenue_per_open_day_eur, net_revenue_eur divided by open_days, rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by store_code from A to Z.
hints: Next, work out each physical store's open days in 2024, counting both its first and its last open day.
Add up each store's 2024 net revenue in its own step before it meets the stores, so every store keeps its one row.
why_this_works: Dividing by the days a store was open, not by every day of the year, lets a store that opened in September stand next to one that traded all year.
